text.p: Ethiopia's foreign ministry said on Tuesday Britain was deliberately misreading the Vienna Convention and all Ethiopian diplomats should be immune from its searches.
But in Nairobi, African diplomats said diplomats anywhere were not immune from searches unless they were in the country where they were accredited or were couriers or accompanying a diplomatic bag.

"The claim by a British diplomat that the Vienna Convention excludes from search only diplomats accredited to an embassy in the country they were arriving in as well as diplomats accompanying a diplomatic bag or courier is a deliberate misreading," Ethiopia's foreign ministry said in a statement.

"Nowhere does the Vienna Convention say that third countries, in this case Britain, could demand that dignitaries and other persons of diplomatic rank sumbit to physcial search as is being wrongly asserted by the British diplomat", it added.

An Ethiopian foreign ministry official said on Monday the government in Addis Ababa had barred its diplomats travelling to Britain without foreign ministry permission because British authorities had violated diplomatic privilege through searches.

A spokeswoman at the British embassy in Addis Ababa said on Monday the Vienna Convention excluded from searches diplomats accredited to an embassy in the country they were arriving in as well as diplomats accompanying a diplomatic bag or couriers.
She said holders of diplomatic passports not accredited to a mission in Britain, not accompanying a diplomatic bag or who were not couriers could be searched under the convention.
"We regard airport security as a legitimate concern but abide conscientiously to the Vienna Convention," she added.
